The length of a tag shall be two bytes.

The tag shall consist of • reserved (Bit 7 of the first byte) • wire type (Bit 6-4 of the first byte) • Data ID (Bit 3-0 of the first byte and bit 7-0 of the second byte) Bit 7 is the highest significant bit of a byte, bit 0 is the lowest significant bit of a byte.

The lower significant part of the Data ID of the member shall be encoded in bits 7-0 of the second byte of the tag. The higher significant part of the Data ID of the member shall be encoded in bits 3-0 of the first byte.
The wire type shall determine the type of the following data of the member. The value shall be assigned as shown in Table 7.9.

SOMEIPTransformationISignalProps . isDynami- cLengthFieldSize is set to true, the transformer shall use wire types 5,6,7 for serializing complex types and shall chose the size of the length field according to this wire type.
A deserializer shall always be able to handle the wire types 4, 5, 6 and 7 independent of the setting of SOMEIPTransformationISignalProps . isDynamicLengthFieldSize

If a Data ID is defined for an ArgumentDataPrototype or ImplementationDataTypeElement by means of SOMEIPTransformation- ISignalProps . tlvDataId .id, a tag shall be inserted in the serialized byte stream.

If the datatype of the serialized member / argument is a basic datatype (wire types 0-3) and a Data ID is configured, the tag shall be inserted directly in front of the member/argument. No length field shall be inserted into the serialized stream.
If the datatype of the serialized member/argument is not a basic datatype (wire type 4-7) and a Data ID is configured, the tag shall be inserted in front of the length field.
If the datatype of the serialized member/argument is not a basic datatype and a Data ID is configured, a length field shall always be inserted in front of the member/argument.
The length field shall always contain the length up to the next tag of the struct, but does not include the tag size and length field size itself.
If the member itself is of type struct, there shall be exactly one length field.
If the member itself is of type dynamic length string, there shall be exactly one length field.
If the member itself is of type fixed length string, there shall be exactly one length field corresponding to dynamic length strings.
⌊ DRAFT g If the member itself is of type dynamic length ar- ray, there shall be exactly one length field.
If the member itself is of type fixed length array, there shall be exactly one length field.
If the member itself is of type union, there shall be exactly one length field.
For the serialization of extensible structs and methods the length field shall cover the size of the type field, data and padding bytes if the member itself is of type union.
A member of a non-extensible (standard) struct which is of type extensible struct, shall be serialized according to the requirements for extensible structs.
A member of an extensible struct which is of type non- extensible (standard) struct, shall be serialized according to the requirements for stan- dard structs.
For the serialization of extensible structs and methods no alignment shall be applied.

The transformer shall only serialize an optional member of a struct if the corresponding bit in the availability bitfield is set as follows: (availabilityBitfield[(pos/8)] & (1<<(pos mod 8))) != 0

If an optional member is available in the serialized byte stream, the transformer shall set the corresponding bit in the availability bitfield as follows: availabilityBitfield[(pos/8)] = availabilityBitfield[(pos/8)] | (1<<(pos mod 8))

If an optional member is not available in the serialized byte stream, the transformer shall clear the corresponding bit in the availability bitfield as follows: availabilityBitfield[(pos/8)] = availabilityBitfield[(pos/8)] & ~(1<<(pos mod 8))
If the transformer reads an unknown Data ID (i.e. not con- tained in its data definition), it shall skip the unknown member/argument by using the information of the wire type and length field.

If the transformer cannot find a required (i.e. non-optional) member defined in its data definition in the serialized byte stream, the deserialization shall be aborted with E_SER_MALFORMED_MESSAGE . For examples, please refer to [10].
If an optional member is not available in the received se- rialized byte stream, the transformer shall keep the memory section occupied by this optional element without modification.
